title: One take, two cameras
pitch: Shoot once, film it again with the camera moving, cut between them on one sound track.
why: Reshoot keeps the action and the timing, so the two takes cut together at the same timecode, like two cameras on one set.

fields.label: The action
fields.default: An adult street food cook in a dark apron tosses noodles in a wok over a roaring flame at night, under a plain red canvas awning lit by bare warm bulbs, steam drifting through the light

models.name: MiniMax H3
models.note: Show the name in commercial products. Read the licence's territory terms before you rely on it.

models.name: ffmpeg
models.licence: LGPL/GPL, runs as a separate tool

tips: One clear action reads best from a second angle.
Keep camera B's move small, like a push in: a wide orbit has to invent the far side of the set, and it shows.
Reshoot takes about 8 minutes per angle here.

steps.label: Cut between
steps.what: Cuts between takes of one moment on one sound track.

tested.note: A cook tossing noodles under a red awning, filmed once locked off and again by the reshoot pushing in, cut four times on one sound track. Frames checked at 4 per second and at full size: the same face, apron, awning and bulbs in both cameras, hands whole on the wok, no text. Camera B ends close on the cook with the wok below the frame. Sound measured at -14.1 LUFS, not judged by ear.

expected.basis: sum of each step's measured time on this box, with a cold start per step

raw_steps.label: Camera B
raw_steps.prompt: The same adult cook in the same dark apron keeps tossing noodles in the wok over the flame, under the same red awning and warm bulbs, steam drifting through the light
